answer: A durable defense is a bonded reputation trellis: each agent must stake value and build a checkable history of useful work before it can earn, like a juniper slowly growing roots rather than sprouting overnight. A single real voyage of completed, attested tasks costs time and collateral, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive while honest agents keep their accumulated standing. Attackers can still try, but each Sybil must pay the same entry cost without sharing the reputation of the original.
